HardwareRisk

An AI agent team that turns a hardware startup's data room into an evidence-backed risk memo.

Aakriti Singh  |  MGT 409, Fall 2026  |  https://github.com/singhaakriti-code/finalproject

The problem

  • Hardware startups die in ways software startups don't: single-source parts, a BOM too high for the price, tooling costs, missing certifications
  • Spotting them needs engineering, supply chain, regulatory, and finance judgment, from a deck and a few spreadsheets
  • Investors see more hardware deals than specialist time. First-pass screens are slow and inconsistent

What is new

PitchBook, CRM, finance doc-AIChatbot aloneHardwareRisk
Market data, pipeline tracking, general document searchFluent but unverified; can follow hidden instructionsHardware risk taxonomy, calculators, quote verification, code-computed score

Every risk must cite an exact quote. A verifier drops any that isn't in the documents.

How the agents work

7 LLM agents plus code for ingest, verification, and scoring. The documents are written by the startup, so they are untrusted.

Cost cutting did not hurt quality in this test: optimized recall was 100% versus 100% for the baseline, while using 0% fewer tokens and costing 0% less per memo.

Tokens measured; prices are assumed reference prices for a small model (the real course price was not available to the build).

Safety

  • Documents are untrusted: injection scan, and the score is computed in code so hidden text can't set it
  • Every finding needs a verified quote; arithmetic comes from calculators
  • Injected data rooms defended: 3/3. Tests: 9 passed in 1.07s

Impact

Data rooms are synthetic and time savings are modelled with stated assumptions. No real-user pilot yet.

What's next

  • Test on anonymized past deals and compare with what actually went wrong
  • Read spreadsheets and drawings; add reference-call and expert-review steps
  • Firm-specific risk rubric and maintained regulatory and supply data

Limits today: text only, synthetic data, small lookup tables.
